narr: Two voices, on purpose. The president's: Pezeshkian told the General Assembly on Wednesday that Iran will 'never bow our head, or bend the knee' and is 'ready for dialogue and diplomacy without accepting the language of force', held up the photographs of the assassinated Leader and the Minab schoolgirls, and called the United States 'the victims' maker of terrorists' — the US and Israeli delegations walked out. The soldiers': Safavi, the Leader's military adviser, said any force 'attempting to land in Iran will certainly be destroyed', that Iran's radars follow US warships from the Gulf to the Indian Ocean, and that the strait reopens only when the blockade lifts and Iran's terms are met — Oman, he says, has a mechanism and Washington 'obstructs' it; the Armed Forces promised a reply 'more severe than previous'; Abdollahi: 'no security for aggressors'. Underneath both, the channel is real for the first time since Islamabad: Baghaei confirms 'another round of message exchange and clarification ... through the Qatari mediator' in New York on Tuesday — two hours by his count, three by Trump's, with Witkoff and Kushner across the table — and lists four conditions 'conveyed ... in a manner that leaves no doubt or ambiguity': end the blockade and the 'aggressive actions', end the war on all fronts, release the blocked assets, recognise the Iran–Oman corridor. Rezaei says the same terms went to Qatar and Pakistan; Fars called the Reuters/Kyodo 'reopen in seven days' report 'unreliable and inaccurate'. Nobody in Tehran has claimed the Cape Dao (Sep 23, one Indian seafarer killed) or the LR Stephanie/Al Maryah pair (Sep 21); Al Mayadeen's index, still behind Cloudflare, carries 'IRGC targets 2 ships near Hormuz after repeat US violations' (undated) beside 'Strait of Hormuz closed until Trump, Netanyahu, removed' and 'Iran denies US crossed Hormuz, calls claims fabricated' — the framing is that the strait is Iran's to close and no US convoy has passed. The airline shutdown took effect Wednesday (flights to Turkey, the UAE and China cancelled; Oman, Azerbaijan and Georgia closed their skies); the rial answered at 234,900, weaker by 4,400 in three days. The NPT bill is still paper. ADDENDUM, Thursday 07:00 daily: the soldiers spoke again before Xi sat down — Safavi (Press TV, 09:33 GMT) said new US or Israeli attacks would take the war 'beyond the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz', that Iran keeps control of the strait, and that Chinese vessels may pass; Pezeshkian told Europe to rethink its snapback line; an IRGC official told Al Mayadeen on Tuesday that 'the war is still ongoing, the strait is not open and the US is lying'. At home, the IRGC announced that Brig Gen Hossein Zarifi, head of the Shahid Sajjad base, was killed in an operation at Saravan on Wednesday — no adversary named. Nobody in Tehran has claimed the six missiles at Yanbu and Taif; nobody has confirmed a second round in New York. The rial firmed by 200 to 234,700. ADDENDUM, Thursday 11:00: Tehran put its price in public and its hand in private on the same afternoon. In public, Rezaei (IRIB): seven conditions, the Americans have four to five days, and 'neither the Strait of Hormuz will be opened nor negotiations begin' before they are met; the IRGC's Vahidi and the army's Hatami echoed the president's 'we do not fear war'. In private, by Reuters' count of six sources, a senior Iranian official sketched the phased way out — 'the first [stage] would be to end the blockade and reopen Hormuz' — and regional sources say the transit-fee demand can go into a side attachment because the blockade hurts more than the toll is worth; the same official: 'our fingers are on the trigger'. The Houthis claimed 'dozens' of missiles and drones on Saudi positions at al-Tuwal and al-Daghareer in Jizan (no Saudi confirmation); Moscow's Ulyanov said IAEA inspectors cannot return while Washington threatens daily. The rial firmed to 234,200. Al Mayadeen was not reached (Cloudflare) — no new carry since Tuesday's 'the strait is not open'. ADDENDUM, Thursday 15:00: Tehran claimed its hit and sharpened its threat. The IRGC posted video of the cargo ship burning in the strait — 'at least one projectile struck the violating vessel' — which is the first claim of responsibility for the Cape Dao, the sixty-second UKMTO report and the first death at sea since the El Gaia. By evening the IRGC's Intelligence Unit put every US asset 'on land and water, including US warships' under 'the threat of continuous and sustained strikes' and claimed the Americans are dispersing to Jordan and going underground — intent, not fire. Ghalibaf mocked the ten-year at 5.1% ('the floor two years out … bell-bottoms'); Araghchi asked Europe to 'confront US aggression'; Kata'ib Hezbollah asked Iraqis to break the 'siege'. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Thursday 19:00: Tehran put a clock on the table and widened its threat. Araghchi told reporters in New York that Iran handed the mediators a seven-day plan this week — meet the conditions and the strait opens on the seventh day, then talks toward a final deal; Pezeshkian said out loud that Iran wants the Americans 'back in the MoU before the midterms'. The same evening the deputy foreign minister told Europe its bases 'will not go unanswered', and the Indian seamen's union said the Cape Dao took two torpedoes. The rial held at 234,200. ADDENDUM, Thursday 23:00: by dawn in the Gulf Tehran had hardened its public line without touching the channel. Rezaei: until the conditions are met the strait stays shut 'and we will not negotiate'; an Iranian source called the New York contacts 'workshops to explore positions'; Pezeshkian told Fox that America 'must choose', and that the Houthis answer for themselves. The IRGC's intelligence arm claimed the Americans had been forced to disperse and dig in. Reuters, meanwhile, had six sources on a phased sequence — blockade off, strait open, then the rest — and Tehran ready to park its transit fee. The rial held at 234,200.

Both things at once, from the same podium. On Tuesday Trump told the General Assembly the choice is 'do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly' or a deal, said Iran 'has largely succeeded in disrupting commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz', asked the room to stay 'united in maintaining pressure', and predicted a deal 'right after the election' — then confirmed that his envoys had sat with the Iranian delegation for three hours that day ('a very good meeting, a very productive meeting ... a lot of momentum'). Witkoff and Kushner were in the room via Qatar, with Pakistan and Egypt assisting; The National's read of the road map is a region-wide ceasefire of up to 60 days, a phased reopening and a negotiating timeline inside it, and Trump ruled out lifting the blockade before 'sufficient goodwill' — 'there will come a point when it's too late'. Rubio on Wednesday: a deal 'would involve hard work over a period of time', the president 'has military options'. Treasury did the pressing: Bessent says 80–90% of Iran's external flights are gone since the Wednesday shutdown, financiers will be prosecuted, and the three objectives are 'regime internal conflict, an Iranian uprising, or deal compliance'. CENTCOM said nothing — its index still ends Sep 15: not on the Cape Dao, not on the LR Stephanie or the Al Maryah, not on the IRGC's drone claims — and no US force has been fired on in the seven-day window, which is what took the US pot under the valve on the numbers. Xi arrived Wednesday for talks that centre on Thursday; Washington hopes Beijing leans on Tehran, Trump 'sees no need' for the help. The six Gulf leaders plus Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria and Turkiye heard 'momentum' and produced no framework; the G7 told Iran to stop arming the Houthis. The market priced the week as a bill: the 10-year touched 5.1% Tuesday, gas printed $4.478, Brent fell to $102 on the talks and rose to $105.6 on Safavi. Overhead, four USAF tankers held station over the UAE at 10:10 UTC — the most named US tails on the feed since Sep 16. ADDENDUM, Thursday 07:00 daily: Xi is in the Oval Office with Iran 'in focus' — Washington wants Beijing to lean on Tehran over the strait and wants answers on the intelligence-to-Iran allegation, while the WSJ counts ~1,300 Chinese air shipments of drone and missile parts to Iran through June. The second round with Araghchi that was expected today is not confirmed by 14:00 GMT, and the market read the silence as 'little progress' (Brent $105.4). Reuters/Ipsos has the president at 32%, a career low, with 17% approving on the cost of living — the poll the board missed on Monday, applied now. The Navy's Sep 21 tracker moved the cruiser Princeton and three destroyers out to the Indian Ocean list; CENTCOM has said nothing since Sep 15, but its blockade tally reached 115 redirected vessels by Wednesday. Saudi Arabia's Patriots — one crew Greek — took down six Houthi missiles and a drone aimed at Yanbu and Taif on Thursday morning. ADDENDUM, Thursday 11:00: the same Reuters story carries Washington's answer — a White House official: 'Iran is desperate for a deal, President Trump holds all the cards', the US has 'no need to negotiate' and is content to let 'the inevitable Iranian collapse' play out; Bessent on Fox: a 'cornered animal', and a 'sequencing' of military, blockade and financial pressure that could force capitulation 'within weeks'. At the UN, Bahrain's foreign minister read a statement for some 80 countries demanding the 'full restoration' of navigation in Hormuz 'without delay' and condemning Iran and the Houthis. Adm. Cooper briefed senators behind closed doors; Senator Scott came out saying 'oil is moving through the Strait of Hormuz'. Xi's arrival was cordial — pandas and students — and produced no Iran readout by 18:00 GMT. The market read the phased-deal report first and the White House second: Brent came off its high and still closed the window at $106.9, the ten-year touched 5.16%. Netanyahu took the UNGA podium at 18:04 GMT promising 'surprises'. ADDENDUM, Thursday 15:00: Washington kept its hand free and heard Beijing ask for talks. The Senate rejected the war-powers resolution 49-50 — Collins, Murkowski, Paul and Tillis crossed, Fetterman held — one of its last votes before Nov 3, with Schumer on gas pumps and Kennedy telling the administration to 'escalate or get out'. Xi, in the Oval Office, told Trump the US and Iran should return to dialogue under the Islamabad MoU 'as soon as possible'; Trump called it a 'great meeting' and talked about granite. Netanyahu at the UN: 'we crushed Iran's army, navy, air force and nuclear facilities'. Macron will send 'soldiers, radars and defence systems' to Yanbu. The ten-year closed at 5.11% and the thirty-year at 5.40% on Wednesday; foreign official custody fell $11.4B on the week; Brent $107. ADDENDUM, Thursday 19:00: Washington's answer, so far, is silence from the top and a hard line from the podium. A mediator told CBS the talks are 'positive, but still early'; the White House told NBC that Iran has 'executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz' and told the oil market it has little need to negotiate. No readout on Iran from the Xi state dinner. Brent gave back 0.8% to $105.8 on the phased-deal reports; the ten-year's 5.11% close stands. Saudi civil defence warned Jazan Province and stood the warning down within the hour. ADDENDUM, Thursday 23:00: Washington's only new number was a big one — an unnamed US defense official told Reuters that some 60 ships and 22 million barrels crossed Hormuz on Wednesday, forty of them under US military coordination, the most since July; Reuters could not verify it, CENTCOM said nothing, and the AIS log saw 25 crossings. The White House line stayed 'little need to negotiate'. The Saudis answered the Houthi missiles by calling in the Mecca pact — Turkish and Pakistani chiefs of staff to meet — while Qatar condemned and France sent radars to Yanbu. Brent gave back 1.5% to $105.0; three US tails, a drone and two tankers, were on the feed at dawn.

First, the schedule: no run fired between Sep 21 07:00 and this one — eleven slots, three news days — so this run catches up and says so. Six things are held, more than any run since the gate began, and they pull in opposite directions. The kinetic side: UKMTO #142 — the bulk carrier Cape Dao struck off Oman on Wednesday morning, afire and adrift, one Indian seafarer dead by the embassy's count — is a confirmed act with a death, rung 6, and goes to Sam with its shipping signal; UKMTO's time-late #141 (the LPG tanker Al Maryah, debris, crew safe) is proposed as a rung-5 row with no signal of its own, because it and the now-named #140 (LR Stephanie) are one salvo on one day. The table side: the Sep 22 Witkoff/Kushner–Araghchi session is the first time US envoys and Iran's foreign minister have been in one process since Islamabad, and it is proposed as its own talks-contact entry with a plain double-count note — four items on the same thread are already before Sam; tick one thread entry, not five. A US-side signal is proposed too, flagged as a loose fit because the rule row says 'endorses the corridor / pause' and Washington has endorsed neither. The numbers moved without waiting: the Iran pot fell 6.9 -> 5.8 because nothing has struck an Iranian asset in a week and the talks component now reads 'active'; the US pot fell 7.3 -> 6.7 because no US force has been fired on in a week — a crossing below the valve, written as a number, held as a story; Small Gulf 6.6 -> 6.0 on the same talks reading. Only Saudi–UAE stays above the valve, and the Taif death that keeps it there leaves the window tomorrow. The door: PortWatch finally published Sep 14–20 — 3.1 transits a day, four tankers in seven days, the lowest tanker week on the board — while the AIS counter closed Sep 23 at 15 in / 10 out with 71 hulls inside, the first day over ten inbound since Sep 18, and the 24-hour log shows two LNG tankers out and two crude tankers in: the measured door is tighter, the live door is busier. The bill: the 10-year touched 5.1% on Tuesday, gas $4.478, the rial 234,900. Forty-five items now wait.
